item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 191753
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM PDT Mon Oct 19 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Trudy, located a couple of hundred miles offshore of
west-central Mexico.

South of Southern Mexico (EP94):
Showers and thunderstorms, associated with a trough of low pressure
located several hundred miles south-southwest of Guatemala, remain
disorganized. Environmental conditions appear conducive for
development, and a tropical depression is expected to form around
the middle of this week as the system moves westward to
west-northwestward at around 10 mph, well to the south of the coast
of southern Mexico.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...medium...60 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

$$
Forecaster Adams

item.title: Tropical Storm Trudy Public Advisory Number 26
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM MST Mon Oct 19 2026 
000
WTPZ31 KNHC 192032
TCPEP1
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Trudy Advisory Number  26
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP212026
200 PM MST Mon Oct 19 2026
 
...TRUDY NEARLY STATIONARY AS IT WEAKENS...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 PM MST...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...19.3N 107.9W
ABOUT 160 MI...260 KM WSW OF CABO CORRIENTES MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...40 MPH...65 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...STATIONARY
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1004 MB...29.65 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 PM MST (2100 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Trudy was
located near latitude 19.3 North, longitude 107.9 West. Trudy is
nearly stationary, but is forecast to begin moving to the northwest
over the next 24 hours.
 
Maximum sustained winds have decreased to 40 mph (65 km/h) with 
higher gusts. Further weakening is forecast during the next 48 
hours, and Trudy is forecast to become post-tropical by tomorrow.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 45 miles (75 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1004 mb (29.65 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Trudy are gradually subsiding today along
coast of southwestern and west-central Mexico. Please consult
products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 PM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Evans/Zelinsky

item.title: Tropical Storm Trudy Forecast Discussion Number 26
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM MST Mon Oct 19 2026 
000
WTPZ41 KNHC 192033
TCDEP1
 
Tropical Storm Trudy Discussion Number  26
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP212026
200 PM MST Mon Oct 19 2026
 
Trudy's nocturnal burst of convection has weakened this morning.
Microwave imagery from around 1300 UTC suggests a broad center of
circulation is present, with convection concentrated primarily to
the east and northeast. ASCAT data from around 1630 UTC also
suggested max winds in the 30-35 kt range, with the storm's center
located to the southeast compared to the previous advisory.  The
latest subjective Dvorak intensity analysis from TAFB also reflects
a weakening trend for the storm. Based primarily on the ASCAT data,
Trudy's initial intensity has been lowered to 35 kt.
 
The tropical storm does not appear to have moved much on satellite 
imagery today, and its motion is estimated to be stationary. Trudy's 
lack of motion is driven primarily by light steering flow associated 
with a low- to mid-level ridge centered to its northeast. In 
addition, moderate 20 to 30 kt westerly winds aloft forcing the deep 
convection to essentially remain in place down-shear of the center. 
It's possible that earlier the low-level center tried to reform 
closer to the deep convection. Track guidance suggests that Trudy 
will move very slowly, with most models indicating a westward to 
northwestward motion until the system dissipates. The latest NHC 
track forecast follows a blend of GDMI and HCCA guidance, which 
reflects this slow motion toward the northwest.
 
Trudy is expected to undergo further weakening as it remains in an
environment defined by increasing vertical wind shear, dry
mid-level air, and upper-level convergence. While the storm may
undergo one more round of diurnally-driven convection, simulated
satellite imagery from global models suggest that Trudy will become
post-tropical in 24 hours, before dissipating after another day or
so. The latest NHC intensity forecast hastens Trudy's overall
weakening trend, while holding steady during possible bouts of
convective re-development.
 
Large swells affecting the coast of southwestern Mexico and 
west-central Mexico associated with Trudy are diminishing today.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  19/2100Z 19.3N 107.9W   35 KT  40 MPH
 12H  20/0600Z 19.4N 108.3W   30 KT  35 MPH
 24H  20/1800Z 19.5N 108.9W   30 KT  35 MPH...POST-TROPICAL
 36H  21/0600Z 19.8N 109.3W   25 KT  30 MPH...POST-TROP/REMNT LOW
 48H  21/1800Z 20.2N 109.5W   25 KT  30 MPH...POST-TROP/REMNT LOW
 60H  22/0600Z...DISSIPATED
 
$$
Forecaster Evans/Zelinsky
